title: Structure of the Picard group of a proper curve
statement:
Let $C$ be a proper smooth connected curve over
algebraically closed $k$. The degree sequence

$$
0\longrightarrow\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Pic}(C)\xrightarrow{\ \deg\ }\mathbf Z\longrightarrow0
$$

splits (the degree map is surjective since a $k$-rational point
gives a degree-one class), hence

$$
\operatorname{Pic}(C)\cong\mathbf Z\oplus\operatorname{Pic}^0(C).
$$

proof.text: Install the structure morphism f as C.Over. Connectedness is given by [def-sc-curves]. Finite type implies locally Noetherian, and smoothness gives regularity by [lem-sc-smooth-regular]. The source theorem IsRegular.irreducibleSpace gives irreducibility (the irreducibility part of [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral]). Apply smoothOfRelativeDimension_iff_topologicalKrullDim_eq to the dimension-one hypothesis to obtain SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f. These are consequences, not new assumptions.

Use the source-library homomorphism d = Scheme.picDegreeHom k C, whose value is Multiplicative.ofAdd (f.picDegree L), and whose kernel has carrier f.picZero by Scheme.coe_ker_picDegreeHom [def-sc-pic0]. Scheme.surjective_picDegreeHom supplies g with d(g) = ofAdd 1: its proof chooses a closed point of the nonempty proper curve and uses Scheme.picDegreeHom_ofClosedPoint. Thus the degree-one point argument is retained without the full divisor-class comparison or local-rings package. Define sigma = zpowersHom C.Pic g. The homomorphism power law proves d(sigma n) = n for every integer n.

Set P0 = ker d. Construct e(L) = (d(L), L * sigma(d(L)) inverse), with inverse (n,y) -> sigma(n) * y. The section identity puts the second coordinate in the kernel. Cancellation proves the left inverse; d(y)=1 and the section identity prove the right inverse. Commutativity proves multiplicativity. The first coordinate is definitionally the required degree. For y in P0, d(y)=1 and sigma(1)=1 give e(y)=(1,y), including equality of the subtype coordinate.
